prov.text: The Company had a provision for credit losses of $100,000 during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a release of provision for credit losses of $502,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The Company makes provisions for, or releases of, credit loss expense in an amount necessary to maintain the allowance for credit losses at an acceptable level under the current expected credit loss (CECL) methodology analysis. The Company recorded a net charge-off of $719,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net charge-off of $605,000 for the year earlier quarter. At September 30, 2026, the allowance for credit losses related to loans receivable was 1.10% of loans receivable, the same as at September 30, 2025. Additionally, at September 30, 2026, the allowance for credit losses related to loans receivable represented 150% of non-performing loans, compared to 302% at September 30, 2025.

intro.text: Norwood Financial Corp (the “Company”), a Pennsylvania corporation, was incorporated in 1995 to become the holding company for Wayne Bank (the “Bank”). The Company is a registered bank holding company subject to regulation and supervision by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (“Federal Reserve”). As of December 31, 2025, the Company had total consolidated assets of $2.425 billion, consolidated deposits of $2.183 billion, and consolidated stockholders’ equity of $242.2 million. The Company’s ratio of average equity to average assets was 9.59%, 8.26%, and 8.14% for fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The Company’s ability to pay dividends may also depend on the receipt of dividends from the Bank, which is subject to a variety of limitations under state and federal banking regulations regarding the payment of dividends.
Such loans may constitute the general obligation of the taxing authority or may rely on a specific revenue source which is responsible for the repayment of the debt.
There are additional risks associated with indirect lending since we must rely on the dealer to provide accurate information to us and accurate disclosures to the borrowers.

The Company’s primary sources of liquidity include deposit generation, asset maturities, cash flow from payments on loans and securities and access to borrowing from the Federal Reserve Discount Window, the Federal Home Loan Bank and other correspondent banks.

Under ASC Topic 606, management determined that the primary sources of revenue emanating from interest and dividend income on loans and investments along with noninterest revenue resulting from investment securities gains, loans servicing, gains on loans sold and earnings on bank-owned life insurance are not within the scope of this Topic.
The Company's principal source of funds for dividend payments to shareholders is dividends received from the Bank.
